title: collectReward is publicly-mempool MEV bait: searchers can sandwich a stable-yield-accumulator deposit to capture rewards intended for long-term stakers
rootCause: Public-mempool `collectReward` lets an MEV bot stake immediately before the funding tx lands, then withdraw+claim immediately after, capturing a disproportionate slice of the freshly-deposited rewards. The V1 re-anchor (DEDUP-001) materially worsens the sandwich because rewards are concentrated in early blocks after each `collectReward` and decay quickly, making MEV-per-dollar-of-capital larger here than in vanilla MasterChef.
impactSummary: Long-term stakers' effective APY is depressed by the MEV bot's share. Yield-accumulator deposits leak value to MEV searchers rather than the staking pool the protocol intends to incentivise.
preservedDetails: ECON-003 carries the staker-side MEV theft angle, which is distinct from DEDUP-008's funder-side griefing. The 'standard MasterChef behaviour' label that profile §8.10 applies is challenged because DEDUP-001 (V1 re-anchor) amplifies the MEV-per-dollar.
remediation: Whitelist `collectReward` to a trusted funder address; use private/MEV-protected RPC for the stable-yield-accumulator's funding txs; add a withdrawal lock / time-weighted reward share for fresh stakes.
dedupNotes: Kept separate from DEDUP-008 because: same root surface (permissionless collectReward) but distinct economic angle — DEDUP-008 is griefer-side (depress yields), DEDUP-009 is staker-side (redirect yield to MEV). Different stakeholders harmed; the remediations partially overlap (a funder whitelist solves both) but the framing differs.
